critical_aspects: Variation is the raw material for selection | The environment decides which traits survive
core_questions_by_aspect: Variation is the raw material for selection: 5/5 [Critical Aspect question, Contrast Set, Build a Rule, Pattern Break, 3-Tier Question] ;; The environment decides which traits survive: 5/5 [Critical Aspect question, Contrast Set, Build a Rule, Pattern Break, 3-Tier Question]
advisory1_verdict: S8: change condition, comparison ;; S19: comparison, named alternatives
ca_question_text_verbatim: S8: "Natural selection can make a population change — but only if the population already contains something to work with. What is that something?" ;; S19: "It is tempting to say some traits are just "good" and others "bad." But a trait by itself is neither. Dark wings, sharp beaks, thick fur — each one only helps if it fits the place the organism actually lives in. The environment is like a test that keeps changing: it never asks which trait is best in general, only which trait works HERE, right now. So take one single trait — dark coloring — and drop it into two different forests. What decides whether that trait saves the animal or gets it eaten?"
